title: FX conversion
context: Converts cash between currencies for an instant FX trade, charges our 0.15% FX fee, and returns the inverse rate shown on the receipt (source currency paid per unit received). Conversions are only allowed during London market hours.

issues.title: BigDecimal built from a double
issues.why: The double 0.0015 isn't exact, so the fee rate becomes 0.00150000000000000003122… and every fee is computed from that inexact value.

issues.title: Division without a scale

why.java: divide() without a scale throws ArithmeticException when the result doesn't terminate. 100.00 / 117.17 does, so most conversions crash.
why.kotlin: Kotlin's / on BigDecimal calls divide(other, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN), which keeps the dividend's scale. The amount has 2 decimals, so 100.00 / 117.17 gives 0.85 instead of 0.853461…, and the receipt shows a wrong rate.

issues.fix: Divide with an explicit scale and rounding mode, for example divide(net, 8, RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN), or a MathContext.

issues.title: Converted amount never rounded to the currency
issues.why: amount × rate has as many decimals as both inputs combined, so the credited amount can have 8+ decimal places that no ledger or bank can hold.
issues.fix: Round once at a defined point to the target currency's fraction digits (Currency.getDefaultFractionDigits: 2 for EUR, 0 for JPY) with a documented rounding mode.

issues.title: Market hours checked in server local time
issues.why: LocalTime.now() uses the server's zone, which is usually UTC, so the window shifts by an hour in British Summer Time. It also ignores weekends and holidays, and can't be tested.
issues.fix: Use ZonedDateTime.now(clock) in Europe/London with an injected Clock, and check a trading calendar for weekends and holidays.

why.java: BigDecimal.equals treats 2.0 and 2.00 as different, so equal amounts are reported as different.
why.kotlin: == calls BigDecimal.equals, which treats 2.0 and 2.00 as different, so equal amounts are reported as different.

issues.title: Currencies as plain strings
issues.why: Typos and unsupported codes such as "usd " or "XYZ" reach the rate provider.
issues.fix: Use java.util.Currency (or an enum of supported currencies) and validate at the API boundary.
